newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares close higher despite unsure outlook.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares close higher despite unsure outlook.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher on Wednesday in an uncertain market nervous about Wall Street's reaction to FOMC's failure to raise U.S. interest rates and unsure of prospects ahead.

"The non-action of FOMC has caused an uncertain mood in the market, which now fears a hefty rate hike at a later juncture. The Danish market is unsure of itself. Tomorrow's trend here will be determined by how Wall Street reacts," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index gained 0.24 point to 121.61 in overall bourse turnover of 736 million crowns. The KFX December future closed untraded at 123.15 point.
Novo Nordisk closed four crowns higher at 910, seemingly unaffected by the general market uncertainty and a Morgan Grenfell profit-taking recommendation.
Tele Danmark was yet again the day's most traded paper, with over 343,000 shares changing hands and ending the day unchanged at 277 crowns.

Carlsberg shed two crowns to 347, while Danisco did better, finishing three crowns up at 325 in the wake of its third sugar beet test of the season for Denmark and Sweden and a forecast that its overall sugar 1996 output would meet EU quotas.
